synopsis: The corpus presents MATLAB/Simulink with the Offroad Autonomy Library and RoadRunner as a complete or near-complete commercial simulation platform; an on-road precedent dated 29 July 2025 used Simulink algorithms with virtual vehicles, sensors and metric-driven tests [f8346, f8373, f1335]. Off-road evidence includes shipped R2026b examples of an autonomous excavator, backhoe truck-loading and open-pit haul truck, alongside an undated Volvo Construction Equipment user story describing a real-time human-in-the-loop excavator simulator built with Simulink and Simscape [f15878, f8391]. The stack provides closed-loop articulated-steering dynamics and controller models in R2026b, explicitly supported coupling to Mevea through FMI or TCP/IP and to Unreal through the Offroad Autonomy Library, plus tightly coupled real-time targets through Speedgoat and Simulink Real-Time [f8599, f8699, f8700, f8645]. A proposed middle-cost chain combines these tools with Mevea or AGX Dynamics for terrain, hydraulics and machine variants, but RoadRunner itself does not require MATLAB or Simulink [f16162, f8385]. Licensing is annual or perpetual per product and public pricing is quote-only; the unofficial January 2024 Simulink figures of 1,480 annually and 5,920 perpetually are presumed US dollars and indicative only, not a firm budget basis [f15877, f15880, f16143].
